jacobian_range_followup.finding: An overflowing 2*K*energy denominator silently zeroed a dimensionless positive Jacobian and could suppress the cut weight.
jacobian_range_followup.correction: Cancel Emax analytically; evaluate (1/(2*K))/hypot(sin(p),kp*cos(p)), reflecting p before trigonometry to retain the soft endpoint mass; reject nonpositive/nonfinite results.
jacobian_range_followup.regression: Old header fails native64/80/128. Tests check the independent 100-digit midpoint Jacobian, both tiny-mass endpoints, and cut m0, m1/J, density*J at J=max/{8,10,12,16}. Existing physical-control tolerances unchanged.
jacobian_range_followup.sanitizer_retry_scope: All 23 numerical tests passed initially; the Async example timed out at60s without diagnostics. The unchanged binary passed in1.84s on retry. The initial timeout log is retained; no cause is asserted and no timeout/suppression was changed.

Parent independently passes 25 native/39 wide/30 sanitizer checks. Earlier finite-q wide/sanitizer checks are preserved under their original checkpoint; no new full precision-matrix claim.

gaussian_range_followup.finding: For finite negative omega, omega-energy can overflow before division by width, silently replacing a representable Gaussian tail with zero.
gaussian_range_followup.correction: For omega<0, use omega/width-energy/width, whose terms have opposite signs and no cancellation; retain (omega-energy)/width otherwise. Energy and width are positive. No normalization, physical kernel, quadrature order or existing tolerance changes.
gaussian_range_followup.regression: The identical extreme-range regression fails the old header in binary64, native 80-bit extended precision and binary128. At J=max/16, width=max and omega=-max, require a positive tail and compare J*density with the J=1, width=16, omega=-16 control. Zero and positive frequencies are controls. MPFR128/256 additionally checks negative-frequency exchange scaling at J=1e1000 and retained precision; these MPFR cases are not exponent-overflow reproducers.
gaussian_range_followup.scope: Focused existing CMake builds, numerical suites and Async example; configured providers at the recorded Uni20 revision. GCC13 native/wide and Clang19 ASan/UBSan, two compiler jobs per lane, BLAS/OpenMP threads=1. Existing sanitizer suppression policy. No fresh full repository build or new Python benchmark claimed.

gaussian_underflow_followup.finding: exp(-x*x/2) can underflow before multiplication by a large Gaussian normalization; representable tails are silently zeroed.
gaussian_underflow_followup.correction: Form sqrt(normalization)*exp(-x*x/4), then square. This retains representable tails without cancellation between logarithms or an additional transcendental call per frequency. Existing finite-normalization rejection is retained.
gaussian_underflow_followup.reference: Complete order-8 two-spinon cut at Delta=2, k=1.5, width=J. Original exp(-x*x/2) expression evaluated with MPFR256 and MPFR384 at the previous head; MPFR exponent range keeps that independent arithmetic path representable. Regression constants use the MPFR384 results.
gaussian_underflow_followup.regression: Identical new tests fail the old header in native64/80/128 at their own exponent limits; MPFR128/256 controls pass. Corrected tests require positive tails and compare relative errors, so absolute tolerances cannot admit zero. Existing physical controls and tolerances are unchanged.
